This page gives what the poster leaves out: the full chip, the CG algorithm step by step, how each number was measured, every value behind poster Figures 3–7, and the terms the poster uses. Sections 1–2 and 4–8 follow the poster's figures in order. All numbers come from one bitstream (build 36) running on the board.

1Architectureposter Figure 1

SPECTRA runs on an AMD KCU116 board, whose Kintex UltraScale+ XCKU5P field-programmable gate array (FPGA) is clocked at 124.97 MHz. The whole bitstream uses 180,739 lookup tables (LUTs, 83.3 % of the device) and 786 DSP blocks, the FPGA's hard multipliers. Poster Figure 1 draws only the blocks that the experiments use; Figure S1 draws the full chip.

The host reaches the chip over JTAG, the board's debug link, through a JTAG-to-AXI master (AXI: Arm's on-chip bus standard), and writes the chip's registers through a memory-mapped input/output (MMIO) crossbar. A RoCC (Rocket custom coprocessor) wrapper exposes the same registers to a RISC-V core. All engines share a 128 KiB global buffer (GLB); a direct memory access (DMA) engine moves data between the GLB and the off-chip DDR4 memory, and an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) input feeds samples to the chip.

Inside the blocks the poster shows, the segmented FFT runs on eight radix-2 single-delay-feedback (R2SDF) lanes, and the pointwise pool runs the CG vector updates as AXPY jobs (y ← a·x + y). The chip also holds five engines that the experiments do not use: a 4 × 4 systolic mesh for sparse matrix multiply (WCSR: wavefront-coherent sparsity reconciliation), a block-scaled mixed-precision engine (MX: FP4, FP8, INT8 and BF16 formats), an im2col convolution engine, a phase-binned adjoint engine (PBA) and a line-DC (data consistency) engine that updates the image one k-space line at a time.

2Method: CG as one stored programposter Figure 2

SPECTRA reconstructs the image x from the measured data y by regularized least squares. The conjugate-gradient (CG) method minimizes this cost by solving the normal equations

(EHME + λI + μDHD) x = EHMy

where E is the encoding operator, M the sampling mask, D the Laplacian, λ and μ the regularization weights, and the superscript H the conjugate transpose; Section 9 lists every symbol. E maps the image to the measured data and includes the off-grid field effects, so a plain FFT cannot invert it.

The chip stores the whole CG loop as one program of 83 descriptors, each an engine job. One doorbell, a single register write by the host, starts the program; the ring sequencer then replays the eight steps of Figure S2 on every iteration. Step 7 tests the residual on the chip and stops the solve, so the host only waits for the result. Figure S3 gives the same eight steps as equations.

3How each number is measured

  • Engine time (measured). A counter on the chip counts clock cycles from the doorbell to the end of the solve. The host reads it over JTAG and divides it by the 124.97 MHz clock, which was checked against the host's timer during the run. Engine time excludes the JTAG data transfers and the one-time table load.
  • Correctness. Every image read back from the board matches, word for word, a software model of the chip's fixed-point arithmetic, and the same model matches the simulated hardware (Verilator).
  • Quality. PSNR = 20·log10(peak of the true phantom / RMS error), with the root-mean-square (RMS) error taken against the true phantom. The reference is a double-precision (float64) CG solve of 10 iterations with the same model, prior and data. Each matrix size has eight scenarios: four phantoms (bars, disks, Shepp–Logan, smooth) at two noise levels (20 and 10 dB SNR), with half the k-space lines sampled and one fixed random seed.
  • Host time (measured). The median of 30 synchronized runs: NumPy on each CPU, and PyTorch (desktop) or CuPy (Thor) on each GPU, with each GPU call captured as one CUDA graph, its fastest form. Desktop: Intel i7-7700K CPU and NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER GPU; edge: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor.
  • Host energy (measured). Each device's own sensor reports its energy over a 3 s window of back-to-back calls, idle draw included: Intel RAPL (running average power limit) for the CPU package, NVIDIA NVML (management library) for the GPU board, and the input rail (VIN) of the Thor module. Energy per image is that average power times the device's own time.
  • Chip energy (estimated). The KCU116 has no power sensor, so energy per image = engine time × 1.586 W. Vivado's power analysis computes that power for the die alone (no DDR4, I/O or board), driven by the switching activity recorded during the real CG run on the routed netlist. The recorded window covers an 8-iteration solve; the 2-iteration solve with the on-chip stop runs the same jobs and stops sooner, and Vivado's estimates for two such CG solves agree within 1.3 %. The whisker in poster Figure 7 is an upper bound: Vivado's default-activity estimate for the whole design, DDR4 controller, I/O and clocking included, 3.79 W.

4Off-grid encoding correctionposter Figure 3

Poster Figure 3 corrects four off-grid encoding effects (Table 1, Figure S4). Host-sequenced means that the host issues each engine job of the CG loop itself, instead of the ring sequencer. On all four, SPECTRA's PSNR lies within 0.015 dB of the float64 CG.

5Measured 0.3 T scans, M4Rawposter Figure 4

M4Raw provides measured 0.3 T brain scans. We reconstruct slice 9 of subject 1 (M4Raw 2022101101) and subject 2 (2022101204) at 256 × 256 with 4 receive coils, in T1, T2 and FLAIR (fluid-attenuated inversion recovery) contrasts. The board runs a column-wise CG in 32 batches of 8 columns, and each batch's output was checked against the software model.

Measured data have no ground truth, so the reference is the fully converged double-precision solution of the same model, and the error is the normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) against it. Chip only: the column-wise CG followed by a refinement pass that runs on the chip. Host-assisted: the same refinement, with its residual computed by the host. The host-assisted refinement lowers the mean NRMSE from 4.92 % to 1.94 %.

sliceNRMSE, chip onlyNRMSE, host-assisted
subject 1, T16.84 %0.91 %
subject 1, T24.60 %3.42 %
subject 1, FLAIR5.49 %0.77 %
subject 2, T14.56 %1.43 %
subject 2, T23.85 %3.16 %
subject 2, FLAIR4.18 %1.93 %
mean4.92 %1.94 %

6On-chip convergence stopposter Figure 5

The CG scalar unit tests the residual after every iteration and stops the solve once ρ falls below τ (step 7 of Figure S3). The table compares that on-chip stop with 10 fixed iterations on the board, with the concomitant-phase encoding, over the eight scenarios per size of Section 3.

sizemodeengine time (ms)iterationsPSNR (dB)float64 CG (dB)plain FFT (dB)gap to float64 (dB): mean (min … max)
16 × 1610 iterations0.10601019.6919.7018.34−0.014 (−0.139 … +0.018)
16 × 16on-chip stop0.03302–319.7219.7018.34+0.014 (−0.137 … +0.224)
32 × 3210 iterations0.27071020.1820.6819.85−0.499 (−2.749 … −0.041)
32 × 32on-chip stop0.0657220.6720.6819.85−0.016 (−0.082 … +0.018)

At 32 × 32 the on-chip stop takes 4.1× less engine time than 10 iterations and lands closer to float64 (mean gap −0.016 dB against −0.499 dB): ten fixed-point iterations drift away from the float64 solve.

The ring sequencer also takes the host out of the loop. The same 10-iteration 16 × 16 solve, sequenced by the host one job at a time, takes 94,093 engine cycles against 13,246 for one command (7.1×), and 3.82 s against 0.040 s of wall time per image over the board's JTAG link.

7Hardware cost and powerposter Figure 6

Build 36 uses 83.3 % of the LUTs, 43.1 % of the DSP blocks and 46.4 % of the block RAM of the XCKU5P (Figure S8, right). The solve draws 1.586 W, of which 0.458 W is static leakage; block RAM is the largest dynamic component (Figure S8, left).

8Execution time and energy per imageposter Figure 7

For one 32 × 32 matrix with the on-chip stop (2 iterations), SPECTRA takes 0.066 ms and 0.104 mJ: 2.6× faster than the fastest GPU (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER) and 54× less energy than the most efficient one (Jetson Thor GPU).

Each host call is timed with the device synchronized before and after it, and the table reports the median of the timed runs. The power is the sensor's energy difference over a window of back-to-back calls, so it includes the idle draw, and the comparison uses only that total. The idle column is one reading taken before the first kernel. The desktop CPU package drew less power while running this job than in that reading, so an above-idle (dynamic) energy would be negative there, and we do not use it. NVML covers the GPU board only, not the host CPU; the Thor's VIN rail covers the whole module.

Abbreviations

abbreviationmeaning
ADCanalog-to-digital converter
AXIAdvanced eXtensible Interface, Arm's on-chip bus standard
AXPYa·x plus y: the vector update y ← a·x + y
BF16bfloat16, a 16-bit floating-point format
CGconjugate gradient
CLBconfigurable logic block, the FPGA's logic tile
CPUcentral processing unit
DCdata consistency (line-DC: an engine that updates the image one k-space line at a time)
DDR4double-data-rate (fourth generation) memory, off chip
DMAdirect memory access
DSPdigital signal processing block, the FPGA's hard multiplier
FFTfast Fourier transform
FIFOfirst-in, first-out queue
FLAIRfluid-attenuated inversion recovery
FP4, FP84-bit and 8-bit floating-point formats
FPGAfield-programmable gate array
GLBglobal buffer, the on-chip memory all engines share
GPUgraphics processing unit
I/Oinput/output
INT88-bit integer format
IRQinterrupt request
JTAGthe IEEE 1149.1 test port; the board's debug link to the host
LUTlookup table, the FPGA's logic unit
MMIOmemory-mapped input/output
MRImagnetic resonance imaging
MXblock-scaled mixed precision
NRMSEnormalized root-mean-square error
NVMLNVIDIA Management Library, the GPU's power counter
PBAphase-binned adjoint
PRSEphasor-recurrence systolic encoding, the matrix-free off-grid encoder
PSNRpeak signal-to-noise ratio
R2SDFradix-2 single-delay feedback, a pipelined FFT
RAMrandom-access memory
RAMB36one 36 Kb block RAM tile
RAPLrunning average power limit, Intel's energy counter
RMSroot mean square
RoCCRocket custom coprocessor interface of RISC-V cores
SNRsignal-to-noise ratio

VINthe input power rail of the Jetson Thor module
WCSRwavefront-coherent sparsity reconciliation

Symbols in the CG equation and algorithm

symbolmeaning
xthe image being reconstructed (one value per pixel)
ythe measured data (k-space samples)
Ethe encoding operator: image to measured data, off-grid field effects included
Mthe sampling mask: which k-space samples were acquired
Dthe Laplacian (second-difference) operator of the smoothness regularization
λ, μthe regularization weights on the identity and on the Laplacian term
Hthe conjugate transpose (the adjoint: EH maps data back to an image)
pthe CG search direction
q, wthe forward and adjoint FFT results of one iteration
rthe residual: the part of the data the current x does not yet explain
ρ = rHrthe squared residual norm
α, βthe CG step sizes: how far to move along p, and how much of the old direction to keep
τthe stop threshold on ρ

Terms

termmeaning
doorbellone write to a chip register by the host; it starts the whole stored program
descriptor programthe list of engine jobs (descriptors) stored on the chip; the poster's CG is 83 of them
ring sequencerthe on-chip unit that replays the descriptor program and loops it until the stop test fires
host-sequencedthe host issues each engine job itself, instead of the ring sequencer
adjoint / forward FFTthe FFT-based EH (data to image) and E (image to data) of the encoding operator
segmented FFTan FFT split into segments, so one job applies the field-dependent phase of each segment
stencila small fixed neighborhood operation, here the Laplacian term DHDp applied pixel by pixel
pointwise poolthe engines for element-wise vector arithmetic: updates such as x + αp, and dot products
CG scalar unitthe unit that computes the scalars α and β and runs the residual test
warp gatherone pass that resamples a distorted image back onto the regular grid
matrix-freeE is computed on the fly instead of being stored as a matrix
k-spacethe spatial-frequency domain in which an MRI scanner samples its data
concomitant phasethe extra phase that a gradient field's concomitant (Maxwell) components add at low field
B0 inhomogeneityspatial variation of the main magnetic field B0
gradient nonlinearitythe imaging gradients departing from a straight line in space, which warps the image
fixed pointnumbers held as integers with a fixed binary point (here 16-bit), instead of floating point
float64double-precision floating point; the reference CG solve runs in it
convergeda solve run until its residual stops improving
All numbers: build 36 of SPECTRA on the AMD KCU116 board, October 2026. Chip power is a Vivado estimate; host power is measured by each device's own sensor (Section 3).
